claims.text: Controlled annealing can induce an optimal degree of nanoscale short-range chemical ordering in Fe–Co–Ni–Cr–Al high-entropy alloys.
Nanoscale short-range chemical ordering enhances local magnetic exchange interactions.
Enhanced local magnetic exchange interactions sharpen the magnetization response at low applied fields.
Coherent interfaces associated with ordered nanoscale regions support rapid thermal conduction.
Coherent interfaces associated with ordered nanoscale regions suppress hysteretic losses.
The ordered-region microstructure maintains or improves mechanical stability.
The as-cast or homogenized Fe–Co–Ni–Cr–Al baseline has a predominantly disordered matrix with minimal intentional nanoscale ordering.
The proposed intervention applies annealing at 600°C, 750°C, and 900°C for 2–5 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Rapid quenching and slow cooling are proposed as controlled post-annealing variants.
High-resolution TEM, XRD, and DSC can establish that targeted nanoscale ordering developed without deleterious phase segregation.
Controlled annealing forms nanoscale clusters or regions of short-range chemical order within the disordered matrix.
Optimized nanoscale ordering produces a stronger magnetocaloric response than the as-cast or homogenized baseline.
Optimized nanoscale ordering increases the isothermal entropy change at low applied fields.
Optimized nanoscale ordering reduces hysteresis relative to the baseline.
Optimized nanoscale ordering maintains or improves thermal conductivity relative to the baseline.
Optimized nanoscale ordering maintains or improves mechanical stability relative to the baseline.
The degree of nanoscale order should correlate systematically with magnetocaloric performance.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold for Fe–Co–Ni–Cr–Al-based alloys annealed from approximately 600°C to 900°C for 2–5 hours.
Phase segregation or grain coarsening may compete with beneficial nanoscale ordering.
Enhanced nanoscale ordering without a significant magnetocaloric improvement, or without an order–property correlation, would falsify the proposed mechanistic link.
